title: PHIRL: Aligning Learned Rewards with Task Progress for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; two selected simulated reward-hacking scenarios plus a small physical task; one training run per condition acknowledged
sections_checked: §III progress-based reward shaping and PHIRL algorithm
§IV experimental setups, datasets, simulation and hardware results
evidence_note: PHIRL shapes AIRL rewards with progress labels along temporal delta, magnitude, potential and completion. It illustrates two selected Robosuite hacks (lift-drop loop and poke-without-place) and reports 100 simulation evaluation rollouts; crucially, authors state one training run per condition. Kinova brushing endpoint counts pom-poms over 10 episodes. The limitations include finite-horizon/completion-status assumptions and random rather than active selection of annotated demonstrations.

title: How Much Progress Did I Make? An Unexplored Human Feedback Signal for Teaching Robots
review_status: full-text citation-follow-up audit complete; human-feedback signal evaluation, not downstream policy-safety validation
evidence_note: Two online studies and one public-space study involve 116 participants total, including 40 non-expert demonstrations; 34/40 demonstrations ultimately succeed but use varied policies. Progress scores tracked completion, harmless/fixable errors and backtracking in studied tasks. This supports the information content of progress feedback, not a claim that trained robot controllers are physically safe; same author lineage as PHIRL, so not independent replication.

title: ReWiND: Language-Guided Rewards Teach Robot Policies without New Demonstrations
review_status: full-text citation-follow-up audit complete; independent reward-model robustness, simulation policy outcomes, and small real-robot study; limits on reset/success supervision and reward failures
sections_checked: §§3.1–3.2 progress rewards, rewind augmentation, and online RL
§4.1 reward alignment across unseen tasks and failure/near-success/success rollouts
§5 limitations and Appendices B–D experiment details
evidence_note: Independent from PHIRL/progress-feedback authors. ReWiND evaluates reward ordering over selected failure, near-success and success videos on 17 unseen MetaWorld tasks; reports 79% IQM success at 100k steps and five real-robot tasks improving from 12% to 68% mean success after one hour. Not a held-out adversarial exploit/safety benchmark: human resets and success detection are assumed; the paper shows a reward-alignment failure on bimanual dish scrubbing under occlusion/missing bimanual data.
